metadata.title: Factors affecting youth citizenship in accordance with socioeconomic background

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Gyeonggi Education Panel Study (GEPS) and reports a random sample of 6,314 eighth graders, with 5,740 responding (90.0%), and a final analytic sample of 4,785 students matched with parents. The manuscript does not report the use of complex survey weights (e.g., sampling/design weights) or replicate-weight procedures, nor does it name any weight variable. Because the analysis is based on latent class analysis (LPA) and subsequent regression within classes using SPSS and Mplus, the paper does not provide a weighting strategy consistent with ILSA-style complex survey inference. Therefore, weighting is treated as not reported, and results should be interpreted as conditional on the sampled GEPS panel rather than as fully population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are youth citizenship participation scales derived from questionnaire items (cognitive participation and affective-behavioral participation), not PV-based cognitive achievement scores from an ILSA assessment. The study also does not describe any PV generation/combining procedure, consistent with the fact that GEPS citizenship outcomes are direct survey measures rather than ILSA achievement scales.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used GEPS fifth-year data surveyed for eighth graders in 2016, drawing on citizenship items and integrating gender from the first-year data and parent information from the second- to fourth-year data. The initial eighth-grade sample comprised 6,314 randomly sampled students; 5,740 (90.0%) responded. The final analytic sample consisted of 4,785 students matched with parents after excluding cases with missing values from the analysis.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent class distal outcomes: Lower group M=4.18, Middle M=4.27, Upper M=4.28; χ²=23.641, p<.000. Within-class regression (Table 4): adj R²=0.271 (lower), 0.287 (middle), 0.241 (upper).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using GEPS 2016 Grade 8 citizenship participation the study leveraged gender, self-esteem, occupational view, peer support, and reading behavior to model cognitive citizen participation within latent socioeconomic classes, finding that cognitive participation increased with higher family socioeconomic background and that girls, higher self-esteem, occupational view, and peer relations were associated with higher cognitive participation across groups. This indicates that strengthening psychosocial supports and reading/peer-enrichment opportunities for students from lower-SES families may narrow participation gaps in civic engagement, though the study is correlational and based on latent-class/regression rather than causal identification.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent class distal outcomes: Lower group M=3.55, Middle M=3.66, Upper M=3.71; χ²=29.053, p<.000. Within-class regression (Table 5): adj R²=0.250 (lower), 0.253 (middle), 0.253 (upper).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using GEPS 2016 Grade 8 citizenship participation the study leveraged gender, self-esteem, reading behavior, volunteer experience, and student–teacher relationship to model affective-behavioral citizen participation within latent socioeconomic classes, finding that affective-behavioral participation was lowest in the lower-SES group and increased with family socioeconomic background. This indicates that policy and school practice should prioritize supportive teacher-student relationships and structured opportunities for volunteering and reading for vulnerable students to improve real-world civic behaviors, while recognizing that the evidence is observational and does not establish causality.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes youth citizenship participation using the Gyeonggi Education Panel Study (GEPS), focusing on eighth graders surveyed in 2016 (Korea). From an initial random sample of 6,314 students, the analytic sample comprised 4,785 students matched with parents after excluding cases with missing values. The authors first used latent class analysis to classify students into three socioeconomic background groups based on household income and parents’ educational attainment, then compared cognitive and affective-behavioral participation across groups and estimated within-class regression models. Cognitive participation differed significantly by class (Lower M=4.18, Middle M=4.27, Upper M=4.28; χ²=23.641, p<.000), and affective-behavioral participation also differed (Lower M=3.55, Middle M=3.66, Upper M=3.71; χ²=29.053, p<.000). The study reports adjusted R² values around 0.24–0.29 for cognitive and ~0.25 for affective-behavioral models, but it does not report survey weights or any plausible-values framework, limiting generalizability beyond the GEPS sample.
